cells.tense: The adjustment is happening right now, with the pen in your hand.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: Teach somebody the way you were taught a skill you care about, and change one piece of it as you go. Say what you changed and why.
cells.core:
You're reading the room and adjusting in real time — more of this, less of that, a different tone for the person who needs one — and it isn't performance. It comes from somewhere settled. You can hold that one person wants the plain truth and another wants it softened, and you don't have to pick a favorite between them.

The adjustment keeps the pull toward what you want alive, and the way you carry it is what carries it. So hand your version on: teach what you were taught the way you learned it, with one change of your own in it. Say what you changed and why, once. That's how your part stays yours, and how what you're following gets passed on by someone who was actually following.
cells.sheetLine: You adjust without losing the thread you're following.
cells.verb: constantly adjusting to keep the blend right
cells.place: following the pull toward what you actually want

cells.tense: You're bracing for a room that is going to need smoothing over.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Move toward something you want today — a step the smoothing wouldn't take. Let it land however it lands.
cells.core:
The smoothing is running faster than the room. You can feel the argument before it happens, so you round the edges early — a difference softened here, a question left unasked there — and the table stays easy. What's gone quiet is the adjusting you're actually good at. Tuning runs on real signal, and you've been feeding it some things said because they'd be easier to hear.

The pull toward what you want is still there under the smoothing. Follow it once today — a step toward the thing itself, taken before you've checked how it settles with any of the others there. You'll find out something real either way. The step doesn't have to be large, just yours and taken.

cells.tense: You were changing registers place to place long before this, and stopped landing anywhere.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Sit with somebody in something hard and don't repair it — no advice, no matching story. Stay your own size and leave when it's done.
cells.core:
Each place you go has its own key, and you've been switching between them — this one for work, this one for family, this one for the friends who know you well — and it's gone on long enough that nothing holds all of you at once. The pull toward what you want is still there. It just doesn't have a clear line to follow right now.

What steadies this is contact, not more effort. Sit with somebody in the middle of their difficulty and don't repair it — no advice, no matching it with your own. Stay your own size while you're there. Being near someone in it, and staying whole, gives the tuning something solid to sense against, and you can find your key again from there.
cells.sheetLine: You've carried the key to each place. Keep one for yourself.

cells.tense: You're tuning all of it already — the code, the pitch, the room — and calling it just how you are.
cells.act: join the practice the others keep
cells.ask: Join the others in something you've only ever done solo — same activity, one sitting. See what it looks like beside theirs.
cells.core:
You read a room and shift your register to match — slightly louder with one group, quieter with another, different words for different people — and it works, so it must just be how you are. It isn't only how you are. It's something you've gotten good at without deciding to, and there's a version of you that's been steering it the whole time.

What you do well by yourself is probably something other people do together somewhere. Go do it with them — same activity, others beside you. You don't have to tell them you're doing anything special. Just be in it together and see what your own version looks like next to someone else's.
cells.sheetLine: You've been turning the dial without noticing your hand on it.
